title: Common-stage descent of normalized classical realizations
statement: Fix D,l,hl, finite realization families a,b,s, actual finite operations o, their scalar and restriction Coherence h, and normalized Mixed comparison data for every finite coefficient inclusion and locally closed immersion. There exists one Common datum at every independent-universe algebraic closure Omega and geometric base W, and these data have CommonRestriction for every locally closed immersion. The classical stage transitions and associator are precisely o and h; the realization maps and fibre comparisons are the specified finite ones on every common-stage representative. This is a descent assertion for already supplied finite realizations, operations and coherence, not an existence theorem for any of those finite data. Interfaces: [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-common-fibres], [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-common-realization], [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-common-system], [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-common-restriction], [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-common-restriction-data], [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-common-restriction-comparison], [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-coherence]. Additional interface owners: [def-real-lisse-realization-data], [def-per-continuous-rational-realization-data], [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-per-adic-base-stages].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(3),(4), 6.8.14(1), Remark 6.8.15; Weil II (1.1.1)d; original node step 7 and common restriction/fibre descent

proof.text: Take Rational at each finite coefficient field as the classical stage category, and the actual scalar raw functor for each transition. Use the scalar identity and composition isomorphisms of h as unit and associator. Their coherence is checked after postcomposition with the fully faithful finite raw realization, where the normalization fields give the prescribed sf unit and balanced tensor associator. Those satisfy the unit and pentagon equations.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(3),(4), 6.8.14(1), Remark 6.8.15; Weil II (1.1.1)d; original node step 7 and common restriction/fibre descent

proof.text: The finite raw realization functors and their normalized scalar comparisons therefore define a morphism of stage systems. Its descended functor has precisely these objects and common-stage maps. Every represented object is in the common heart because its finite representative lies in the finite heart. For fullness, represent a target arrow over one common larger finite field and use fullness of the finite raw realization there.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(3),(4), 6.8.14(1), Remark 6.8.15; Weil II (1.1.1)d; original node step 7 and common restriction/fibre descent

proof.text: For faithfulness, move equality to a common stage and use faithfulness there. This proves the Hom-colimit bijection. Take the intrinsic common fibre specified by sfAdicCommonFiber_exists and its finite comparisons. Composing each finite comparison with the scalar extension of the finite classical fibre isomorphism defines classical_fibre and proves classical_normalization.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(3),(4), 6.8.14(1), Remark 6.8.15; Weil II (1.1.1)d; original node step 7 and common restriction/fibre descent

proof.text: For a locally closed restriction, take the actual finite restriction functors as stage components. Choose the supplied normalized mixed comparisons for its transition maps, with the inverse orientation required by the stage morphism. The same faithful normalization proves compatibility with the unit and associator. Descend the finite raw restriction comparisons to the pair categories.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(3),(4), 6.8.14(1), Remark 6.8.15; Weil II (1.1.1)d; original node step 7 and common restriction/fibre descent

proof.text: On a representative the descended map is exactly the finite map followed by inclusion, proving finite_comparison. All checks take place at one common finite stage, including ranks zero and empty schemes.
